origins.section: Four Knobs, and Each Solver Names Them Differently
Focus Says Which Side of the Gap to Work On
Defaults Win Here, So Change One Knob at a Time and Keep the Default Unless Both Measures Agree

recorded.prompt:q-common-knob: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-common-knob: The common knob is accepted at every level and changes nothing; HiGHS's own option changes the run.
recorded.prompt:q-focus: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-focus: SCIP's `FEASIBILITY` emphasis did what it says: a plan within 1% with 0.39 of the work, 20 wins and 1 loss. ... It is the right setting for a service that stops at a work limit and reports the best plan
recorded.prompt:q-one-knob: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-one-knob: Two knobs changed together cannot tell you which one did the work.

recorded.rule: Q2 v2: a giveaway, read from the question's own text alone
recorded.prompt:q-common-knob: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. Say which cue decided it, or that none did.
recorded.outcome:q-common-knob: from the question's text alone, the reader picked none; the key is 'b'
recorded.because:q-common-knob: c repeats 'error' but conflicts with 'No error is raised'; no option is clearly longer, more specific or a restatement

recorded.outcome:q-focus: from the question's text alone, the reader picked none; the key is 'd'
recorded.because:q-focus: No cue singles one option out: a, c and d all echo the stem's 'plan'/'sooner' wording and are similar in length; no absolute terms; grammar fits all.
recorded.prompt:q-one-knob: Answer ONLY from this question's own text: its stem and its options. Use no knowledge of the subject at all; treat every term as a word you have never met. Pick an option only when the wording itself singles it out: it is longer or more specific than the others, it repeats words from the stem, the others carry absolute terms such as 'always' or 'never', the stem's grammar fits it alone, or it restates the stem. A cue decides only when it clearly singles out one option over every other; a weak cue, or one another option shares, decides nothing. Otherwise answer 'none'. recorded.outcome:q-one-knob: from the question's text alone, the reader picked none; the key is 'a'
recorded.because:q-one-knob: No cue clearly singles out one option. a and b are the same length and both repeat 'cut the work' from the stem. c and d have the same template, which weakly points to a or b but does not choose between them. Neither 'little or none' nor 'each' is an 'always'/'never' absolute, and the stem's grammar fits all four options.
